question: Is the captured game log deep enough for any luck-based claim?
known: 22 settled finals across 2026-11-13, 11-14 and 11-15, each transcribed from an official game book or the official scoreboard. No team has more than two captured games.
missing: Roughly 150+ finals (four or more per team) before a per-team z-score can be computed at all.
how_to_find: Read https://www.nba.com/games for each earlier date in the 2026-27 season (the season started 2026-10-20) and transcribe each game's official game book from https://statsdmz.nba.com/pdfs/. This is mechanical, not analytical: 1 game book per game.
blocks: Every strategy gate; the luck band; the walk-forward error estimate's precision.

question: Is there a licensed closing-line feed available to this project?
known: No feed is connected. The market-anchor field is therefore null on every line and the model line is published alone.
missing: The identity of a feed, its licence terms, and whether its historical closing lines can be used for the out-of-sample log-loss that the blend weight needs.
how_to_find: Ask the operator which book or aggregator they are licensed to use, then check that the feed exposes historical closing lines, not just live prices. The blend formula is already implemented.
blocks: The market-anchored prior; any comparison of a strategy against a market; any claim that a model price is an edge rather than a restatement of a team rating.

question: Are per-player game logs available for the players on the injury report?
known: The 11/16 09:15 AM ET report names 56 players across 11 clubs. No per-player log is captured for them.
missing: Minutes, points, rebounds, assists and opponent per player per game - the inputs to a minutes-redistribution model and to any player-prop correlation.
how_to_find: The official box score for each game is linked from each game page on https://www.nba.com/games; the game book PDF at https://statsdmz.nba.com/pdfs/ already prints a full per-player line for both teams. One game book therefore yields both the game result and the player logs, which is why the two captures should be done together.
blocks: Player-prop prices; prop-combo rho; the minutes-redistribution model's replacement shares; any injury-impact statement beyond 'these players are listed Out'.

question: Whose jurisdiction governs, and is this a betting product or a research tool?
known: The current build is a research dashboard: it publishes originated numbers and prints no offer, accepts no stake, and labels every price as fair value rather than an offer.
missing: The operator's jurisdiction, and whether any published number crosses the line into 'advising on a bet' there.
how_to_find: The operator names the jurisdiction. If it is the Netherlands, read https://kansspelautoriteit.nl/online-kansspel-aanbieden for the licence requirement. If elsewhere, read that regulator's equivalent before publishing prices rather than projections.
blocks: Any public publication of a price as an offer; any reward or prize attached to a leaderboard; any transfer of money.

question: Does the league's terms of use permit this use of its statistics?
known: NBA.com Terms of Use, section on gambling, places restrictions on the use of NBA statistics for gambling purposes. This build publishes statistics with attribution and no bet acceptance.
missing: Whether a licence or written permission is required for a public dashboard that publishes model prices derived from official statistics, and whether a private research use differs from a public one.
how_to_find: Read https://www.nba.com/termsofuse in full and, if the intended use is commercial, seek written permission. This is a legal question, not a data question, and the build treats it as a blocker on publication of prices rather than on publication of verified statistics.
blocks: Public bet-surface publication; any commercial use; any redistribution of official statistics beyond research quoting.

question: What is the actual injury-report revision cadence, and how stale is acceptable?
known: The official index listed reports every 15 minutes from 12:00 a.m. to 9:15 a.m. ET on 11/16. Teams must designate a status by 5 p.m. local the day before, or 1 p.m. local on a back-to-back game day, and must file a game-day report between 11 a.m. and 1 p.m. local (8-10 a.m. for early tips).
missing: A measured distribution of when statuses actually change relative to tip-off.
how_to_find: Archive every report from the index across several game days, diff consecutive versions (the mechanism exists: scripts/injury_archive.py and the 11/15-to-11/16 delta on this site) and record the timestamp of each status change. The index publishes every version, so the sequence is recoverable.
blocks: The freshness gate's two-hour threshold, which is currently a proposal rather than a measured number; any claim about how much a late status change should move a line.

question: Which venue coordinates may be used for travel distance?
known: Arena coordinates from each building's Wikipedia article are captured for all 30 arenas and every distance names the article it used. They are a secondary source, not an NBA value.
missing: An official or licensed coordinate source, or the operator's acceptance of the secondary one.
how_to_find: Ask the operator whether a secondary source is acceptable for a labelled secondary metric. If an official source is required, the league's media guides print venue addresses, which can be geocoded, but that is still a derivation from an official document rather than an official coordinate.
blocks: Travel distance's elevation from 'secondary' to a published fact. The distance is printed today with its tier stated.

question: What does a founding-season baseline look like, and is this season's spread unusual?
known: The official team pages show 2026-27 win totals from 12-2 (LAL, SAS) to 1-13 (MIL, UTA) after ~14 games.
missing: Prior-season team ratings and the league's historical home-win rate, so today's 0.591 measured home rate can be placed against a baseline.
how_to_find: Read the same three official team pages with Season=2025-26 and Season=2024-25, which are published and selectable in the page's season control.
blocks: Whether the pinned home-court value of 4.12 points is normal or an artefact of 22 games; any shrinkage target that uses a historical league mean.

question: Is the ATL@MIL quarter-score contradiction in the PDF a transcription artefact or in the official document?
known: The captured block prints Q3 as 37 in the SCORE BY PERIOD table and 27 in the same document's recap line; 37 gives a sum of 116 against a printed final of 106, 27 gives 106. The nba.com scoreboard shows a final of 106-113.
missing: Whether the table itself is wrong or the PDF text layer reordered the digits.
how_to_find: Open the same game book at https://statsdmz.nba.com/pdfs/20261115/20261115_ATLMIL.pdf and read the period table directly, then compare with the box score at https://www.nba.com/game/atl-vs-mil-0022600243/box-score. If the table is right and the final is wrong, the league has an errata process; if the table is wrong, this is an extraction artefact and the row can be settled from the box score once the operator approves that as a tie-break.
blocks: Settlement of that one row. It does not block any other row: the other eight finals are settled.

question: How should a strategy's reward tier work without a jurisdiction decision?
known: The build has a tier concept (T1 funded to T5 blocked) and currently funds nothing, so the question is not yet live.
missing: Whether rewards are a prize contest, a pooled stake, or an internal score; the Dutch and other regulators treat these very differently.
how_to_find: This is Q04's decision restated for the leaderboard rather than the picks page. It cannot be answered from data.
blocks: Any public leaderboard that attaches a reward; any staking rule.

question: Are the two estimators independent enough for their disagreement to mean anything?
known: They share no input: A reads final margins only, B reads the official advanced page only. The pinned home-court term is common to both, but it is a measured league constant rather than a fitted parameter.
missing: A measured correlation between A's error and B's error across a large sample. That is the actual test of independence, and 25 forecasts is not enough to run it.
how_to_find: Once the game log is deep enough (Q01), regress A's and B's forecast errors on each other game by game. If the correlation is high the two estimators are not independent and the disagreement number would need to be recomputed on orthogonalised residuals.
blocks: The interpretation of the disagreement column as a confidence signal. Today the site claims only that the inputs are disjoint, which is verifiable from the code, not that the errors are uncorrelated, which is not yet measured.

question: Should the totals model be A's total or B's total?
known: The two methods disagree by up to ~10 points on individual games (POR@MIN: 237.1 vs 227.4). Neither has been scored out of sample, because only 22 finals exist and the totals benchmark needs the same walk-forward discipline the margin model uses.
missing: A walk-forward totals benchmark on a deeper log - the same shape as the margin model's report - so the better method can be chosen on evidence rather than preference.
how_to_find: Extend the game log (Q01), then score both totals methods game by game against the actual final total, using strictly earlier games for each prediction.
blocks: Publishing a single total as THE line. Today both are printed side by side with the delta, which is honest but not yet a decision.
